podcast.title: Cultural Phenomenon & Drag Anthem
podcast.body: Originally released in 1977 as a "kitschy standout" dialogue-driven story song (titled in "classic seventies, me-decade-fashion"), it initially peaked at number 97. After Charlene had given up recording and moved to the UK, Tampa DJ Scott Shannon began playing it "almost as a joke" in 1982, but listener response was "unironically strong." Shannon's advocacy led Motown to relocate and re-sign Charlene, re-releasing the single which climbed to number three. Listeners at the time regarded it as an "earnest farewell to the excesses of the 70s." More than a decade later, it became a drag anthem by soundtracking the opening scene of "The Adventures of Priscilla Queen of the Desert," ultimately defining Charlene's career. "The reissued I've never been to me single climbed all the way to number three in 1982."

podcast.body: This song was ranked #4 on a 2006 CNN poll of the worst songs of all time. It was the only song from the 1980s to appear on this particular list.
